title: Polygons: the circle of a periodic or line-arrangement law and its pi
claim: Circles of periodic and line-arrangement parity laws are polygons. (1) For the parity law on a doubly periodic plane graph G (one parity knot per vertex, variables on edges; G 3-edge-connected, G and its dual G* locally finite, G* 2-connected), |bond distance - 2||x||_P| <= C, where P is the velocity polygon of G* (convex hull of displacement/length over cycles of G*/Z^2): the circle is half P, a centrally symmetric polygon with rational vertices in lattice coordinates, and its Golab pi (half the self-perimeter) is rational and lies in [3, 4]. (2) By Niven's theorem the only affinely regular circles of periodic laws are parallelograms (pi = 4) and hexagons (pi = 3); no periodic law has an elliptic circle. (3) For the law with a four-place parity knot at each crossing of a simple arrangement of lines in k >= 2 directions with unit normals n_j, densities rho_j and bounded discrepancy, 2 sep(s, t) + 3 <= bond distance <= 2 sep(s, t) + C (2 sep + 1 on one line), sep counting the lines strictly separating s and t; so bond distance = 2 sum_j rho_j |<x, n_j>| + O(1) and the circle is half the polar of the zonotope sum_j rho_j [-n_j, n_j]. n equiangular equally dense families give a regular 2n-gon with pi = 2n sin(pi/2n) (n odd) or 2n tan(pi/2n) (n even), Archimedes' inscribed and circumscribed values, irrational for n >= 4 and tending to the Euclidean pi; such an arrangement is doubly periodic only for n = 2, 3; the Penrose pentagrid law has pi = 5/phi. (4) Computed exactly: the 19 distinct laws on the 11 Archimedean and 11 Laves tilings have pi in {3, 10/3, 16/5, 7/2, 11/3, 4}.
failure_conditions: A doubly periodic law whose bond distance minus twice the graph distance of the dual grows without bound.
A periodic law whose circle polygon has a vertex with an irrational lattice coordinate, or whose pi is irrational.
A segment pair of a line-arrangement law whose bond distance is below 2 sep + 3 (2 sep + 1 on one line) or exceeds it by an amount growing with distance.
foundation_claim_scope: Doubly periodic plane graphs with locally finite 2-connected duals (Theorem 1, Corollary 2); simple line arrangements with finitely many directions, positive densities and bounded discrepancy (Theorem 3, Corollary 4); the 19 laws on the 11 Archimedean and 11 Laves tilings computed exactly.

validation.status: prose proofs of Theorems 1 and 3 and Corollaries 2 and 4; check.py (18 s) verifies the 22-row exact table, Karp support functions, exact bond distances on patches (excess 0.1 to 8.7 out to 2||x|| = 242), line arrangements (n = 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 and a Penrose pentagrid) and regular-polygon pi, with four rejected controls; no human or external review
validation.novelty: known-overlap-found: velocity polygons of periodic graphs (Fritz 2013; Kotani-Sunada; Eon), Golab's theorem, self-perimeters of regular polygons (Martini et al.), partial cubes of line arrangements; the delta is the reduction of bond distance to dual graph distance and to separating lines, the rationality of pi for periodic laws with Niven's corollary, and the exact table.
